modules.module_title: Analyse transport data and generate reports

pcs.pc_description: Collect all the necessary information from sources such as ERP, fleet management software, GPS trackers, order management systems, and driver logs.
Organise the collected data by type e.g. Operational data, financial data, customer data, and traffic-related data. Check for data accuracy and consistency.
Analyse the transportation performance based on delivery times, routes, the use of vehicles, consignment type, geography of movement, in- house or outsourced vehicle, client-wise performance, etc.
Identify patterns, such as frequent delays on certain routes, underutilized trucks, or high costs associated with specific trips.
Prepare vehicle capacity utilisation rates for different types of vehicles and geographies and identify the root cause of under-utilisation, if any
Compute workforce capacity utilisation and productivity rates and identify reasons for under- utilisation, if any
Check route variations during trips and report the impact on cost, delivery timeline and reasons
Review the financial data—fuel consumption, tolls, maintenance costs, and driver wages to calculate cost-per-mile or cost-per-delivery.
Check the repair and maintenance of vehicles and report vehicles which are incurring maintenance costs beyond acceptable limits
Identify trends and insights from the data, such as consistent delays during peak hours, recurring maintenance issues with certain vehicles, or negative customer feedback.

Prepare the report structure and include key findings and recommendations, along with a data overview, analysis, costs, trends, recommendations and suggestions for improvements, such as route optimisation, cost-cutting measures, or technological investments.
Generate the report using clear tables, charts, or graphs to present the data findings visually and share them with management.
Define the Objective of Trend Analysis e.g. delivery times over the past six months to identify peak delays.

Identify which metrics or variables to track for trends such as delivery timelines, dispatch delays, product damages, insurance claims, vehicle utilisation, workforce utilisation, fuel consumption, vehicle maintenance, etc.

Visualise data trends by using time series graphs, moving averages, and bar/line charts to illustrate changes over time and highlight long-term patterns, such as delivery times or fuel costs across months or routes.
Review the visualisations to identify trends, patterns, or anomalies and Compare trends across different segments.
Apply statistical methods to quantify trends and Interpret the Results.
Summarise the findings in a report, highlighting key insights, areas of concern, non- compliance and submit to management.

modules.module_title: Follow-up with internal team and external stakeholders

pcs.pc_description: Provide internal teams (e.g., warehouse, customer service) with timely, accurate shipment details, including delivery schedules, special handling requirements, and tracking information.
Communicate precise instructions to external vendors (e.g., drivers or third-party logistics providers) about delivery locations, timelines, and any specific client needs.
Stay in close contact with internal teams to monitor daily operations, resolve any issues, and ensure everyone is aligned with the transportation plan.
Track vendor performance in real-time to ensure deliveries are on schedule. If there are delays or issues, communicate with the vendors quickly to find solutions.
Share performance reports, delivery statistics, and any updates regarding transportation challenges or improvements with relevant stakeholders.
Build strong, professional relationships with vendors by offering regular feedback, discussing expectations, and negotiating terms to ensure a long-term, mutually beneficial partnership.
Liaise with external vendors to address any delivery problems, such as missed pickups, route issues, or damaged goods, and work together to resolve these challenges efficiently.
Ensure external vendors are compliant with any legal or regulatory requirements (e.g., delivery hours, vehicle maintenance), and follow up to ensure these standards are met.
Provide stakeholders with timely updates on any shifts in delivery schedules, changes in customer requirements, or other logistical changes.
Coordinate with the customer right from the pickup, transit and till delivery of consignment as per plan
Keep clients informed of delivery timelines, any potential delays, or changes to the agreed schedule.
Communicate to the point of contact from the customer side in case of any mismatch/ deficiency in documentation & any other update regarding shipments
Liaise with customers for damaged goods during handling/ transit for claims processing and replacement
Escalate to the customer in case the transporter is nominated from the customer side for delayed pickups, lack of coordination, etc.
Resolve client complaints or issues promptly and implement improvements to ensure higher satisfaction in future deliveries.
Make a note of any special cargo movement/packaging requirement
Provide delivery status notification to consignor/ consignee and submit the invoice
Foster strong relationships with clients by providing exceptional service, handling complaints efficiently, and always following up to ensure satisfaction.

modules.module_title: Perform route optimisation and feasibility assessment

pcs.pc_description: Define the specific goals and constraints that need to be considered when planning the route, such as Delivery time, Cost optimisation, Cargo type, Vehicle limitations, Safety considerations, etc.
Collect data about the potential routes that can be used, which may include Road types, Traffic patterns, Road conditions, Weather conditions, Legal or regulatory restrictions, etc.

Review the data collected on point of origin, point of destination, type of goods, pickup date and time, delivery date and time, volume of goods, vehicle capacity, vehicle traffic constraint and transporter details
Assess the costs associated with each route by considering factors such as fuel costs, tolls and fees, vehicle wear and tear, etc.
Evaluate how long each route will take and if the proposed routes can meet the required delivery time.
Ensure the routes comply with local regulations, like Weight limits, Size limits, Permits, Environmental restrictions, etc.
Use Route Optimization tools or software such as Google Maps, API or OptimoRoute to automatically calculate the best routes based on objectives (cost, time, fuel efficiency).
Input all the gathered data (traffic, weather, road conditions) into the software for real-time route adjustments.

Review multiple route options and analyse the pickup and delivery sequence for the optimal time, allocation of loads, Safety, Risk Factors, and vehicle capacity collected from the route planning software
Plan optimised routes for multiple depots, ensuring cost efficiency across the whole operation and Evaluating the Impact of Alternative Routes (if needed).
Perform lane analysis to identify the efficient routing option and to understand the feasibility of the Over Dimensional Cargo (ODC) vehicle to transport the cargo through the identified route
Finalise the transportation plan, considering all assessments and various factors such as tolls, rest stops, driver shift changes, vehicle relays, vehicle refuelling, etc.
Approve the plan for daily truck coverage, driver and trip assignment
Make sequential plans for alternate routes based on the routing analysis for contingency requirements like inclement weather, natural calamities, etc.
Communicate with the internal team to finalise the route plan and get it approved by the manager
Inform all stakeholders (drivers, logistics teams, customers) of the chosen route and any contingencies.
Brief the transporter on the key areas of concern and the preparedness required during transit
Implement the route plan and monitor the shipment in real time for any required adjustments.
Track the actual performance of the route against expectations after the delivery.
Review actual delivery times versus estimated times and the overall cost of the route and compare it with budgeted costs.
Gather feedback from drivers about road conditions, delays, and overall route efficiency.
Regularly identify and analyse bottlenecks or inefficiencies in the route optimisation process.
Re-evaluate routes periodically based on updated data and conditions

Conduct a review of the route’s performance to determine if there were any deviations from the plan (e.g., delays, unexpected road closures) after each delivery or at regular intervals for continuous improvement.

modules.module_title: Track and report progress in real time

pcs.pc_description: Use GPS and telematics systems to track the location, movement and status of each vehicle in real-time.
Send alerts about potential hazards on the road, weather conditions, and real-time traffic patterns to prevent theft, avoid shipment delays, and minimise revenue loss for drivers.

Render relevant, comprehensive, accurate, and real-time information to the stakeholders and drivers using the Telematics Control Unit (TCU), including vehicle routes, performance data, speed limits, engine idle time, and any customer requests.
Monitor driving behaviours such as overspeeding, excessive braking, fuel efficiency, rapid acceleration and excessive idling.
Track and report key metrics for drivers, such as speed, braking patterns, acceleration, and cornering.
Take note of the temperature in the reefer vehicle, trigger the alarm and alert the driver in case the temperature falls below the required level
Check on the weather and traffic of the area next to be crossed and Re-plan the route or reschedule the delivery in case of any anomalies
Monitor where each vehicle is and make route adjustments to avoid delays or traffic congestion.
Assign deliveries to the closest available vehicle, improving response time.
Use telematics data to monitor and mitigate risks associated with fleet operations, including accidents, theft, and unsafe driving.

modules.module_title: Use telematics to support fleet operations

pcs.pc_description: Collect real-time data from vehicle fleets using a cloud-based server connected to installed telematics systems and generate daily reports on vehicle and cargo information.
Collect and analyse performance data from Telematics systems to identify trends and areas for improvement.
Populate reports with details of the vehicle carrying the cargo, such as vehicle type, vehicle number, driver name and contact details, license and permit details, details of the cleaner, etc.
Track the health of vehicles, identify potential issues, and schedule preventive maintenance through a service reminder forecasting dashboard.
Monitor fuel consumption through telematics systems to identify fuel usage inefficiencies.
Use telematics to monitor compliance with driving hours regulations, speed limits, and other legal requirements.

pcs.pc_description: Perform spending analysis with all forward and reverse costs considered.
Populate data from different software like TMS, fuel purchasing systems, truckload carrier accounting systems, customs, bill of lading data, and any others.
Collect trucking spot freight rates, contracted freight trends, current truck equipment orders, and outbound and inbound data.
Compare findings to industry trends.
Prepare a scorecard and use the same for easy comparison of carrier performances based on different factors.
Substantiate findings using facts-based analysis and quantification of exposures.
Assess the effectiveness of business monitoring procedures and processes.
Shift from stagnant or point-in-time reviews to focused implementation of ongoing monitoring.
Analyse company stock and location data for optimal routing.
Identify ways to optimise "less than truckload" shipments. Inefficient truck utilisation leads to revenue leaks.
The capacity of freight vessels and trains should be utilised at least at a rate of over 70% per trip in order to maintain profitability.
Identify high-risk business areas, products, freight carriers, business lines, and geographies to focus efforts.
Analyse overall freight expenses to identify anomalies.
Utilise available infrastructure to the maximum.
Collate data from tracing and analyse the same for patterns on transit time, delays and service failures.
Allocate full capacities to orders, and plan transportation itineraries and frequency.
Provide insights to the management by developing a deeper understanding of freight expenses to identify opportunities for improvement with (efficiency and control environment).
Use a route optimisation solution to optimise delivery routes around changing traffic conditions.
Use a transportation planning solution that integrates supply chain planning and shipping execution to assess real-time risk across the supply chain.
Integrate a shipment planning window with TMS that covers projection for several days forward and order management, procurement, and supply chain optimisation solutions.
Use technologies like weatheroptics to forecast and enhance the solutions for risks related to weather conditions. This allows rerouting of vehicles to minimize the impact of weather hazards.
Choose carriers with better vehicle maintenance and safety records, which reduces the risk of transit delays due to vehicle breakdowns.
Integrate digital freight markets and brokerages into TMS, which will help optimise cost and analyse the quotes.

Choose vendors with APIs for posting loads, booking, tendering, and tracking. Carriers using digital fleet management and TMS solutions with highly automated material handling reduce the risk of lost shipments.
Identify alternate ports and CFS/ ICDs, which decrease the risk of delay. Build agility into processes so that switch ports are available if needed.
